answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable stake. When an agent registers, it locks a deposit and publishes a public commitment; peers attest work only after checking it against a shared ledger. Creating thousands of fake identities then requires thousands of deposits, while honest agents reuse one. Like carving a name into marble rather than whispering it in a crowd, the record is durable and costly to forge. Even if an attacker paints over it with umber, the stake and history remain auditable, so fake votes dilute and honest reputation compounds.
